subject: writing
note: Rubrics for open-ended writing, graded by Claude on the Home Assistant side via the grading webhook (Fofa.grade). Each rubric is passed as `detail.rubric` in the grade-request payload; HA prompts Claude to score the student's `detail.response` against it and return { ok, score, max, feedback }. See MEASURABLES.md.

rubrics.title: Show, don't tell
rubrics.prompt: Rewrite the sentence "She was scared" without using the word scared — show it through what she does, senses, or notices.
criteria: Avoids the stated feeling word and its obvious synonyms (1 pt)
Uses a concrete action, sensory detail, or physical reaction (1 pt)
The feeling is clearly inferable from the details (1 pt)
Reads smoothly as one grammatical sentence (1 pt)
rubrics.feedbackStyle: Warm and specific; name one thing that worked and one concrete next step. Address the student by name if provided.

rubrics.title: Topic sentence
rubrics.prompt: Write a topic sentence for a paragraph about why recess matters.
criteria: States a single clear main idea (1 pt)
Is a claim that a paragraph could support, not just a fact (1 pt)
Is complete and correctly punctuated (1 pt)
rubrics.feedbackStyle: Encouraging; if it's a fact rather than a claim, show how to turn it into one.

rubrics.title: Sensory detail
rubrics.prompt: Describe your favorite place using at least three of the five senses.
criteria: Uses three or more distinct senses (2 pts)
Details are concrete rather than generic (1 pt)
Word choice fits the mood of the place (1 pt)
rubrics.feedbackStyle: Celebrate vivid details by quoting one back; suggest one more sense to add if fewer than three.
